2012 Chevy Camaro ZL1 With One Owner in the Papers for Sale, Muscle Car Looks Great
15 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
The Camaro story may have ended almost three years ago, but General Motors, which is Chevrolet’s parent company, is apparently interested in bringing it back.
Word on the street is that the next-gen Camaro could be offered as a four-door sedan strictly, presumably with V8 firepower, and maybe an optional stick shift. It remains to be seen whether this is true or not, but meanwhile, those who want a Chevy muscle car must search the used market for that perfect example.
And if the fifth generation gets your heart racing, then you have come to the right place, because you have the chance to buy the one pictured in the gallery. This machine has a single owner in the papers who bought it new in May 2012. The man paid $60,384 for the car, as per the attached window sticker, and has put 32,000 miles (51,500 km) on it.
Thus, it is not a high-mileage example, and the fact that it has a single owner in the papers definitely makes it more appealing. But there are some downsides, as this Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 has a check engine light on, some wear on the driver’s seat, chips on the front bumper, and scratches on the rear one. It was also involved in an accident in February 2019, sustaining “minor damage” to the rear end.
Photo: Cars&Bids Moreover, it also has extensive modifications . It features a 416-cubic-inch LSA V8 long block engine under the hood with a Kong Performance supercharger. It also has new ported and polished cylinder heads, a new camshaft, an LSA crankshaft, a new oil pump, and upper supercharger pulley, lower crank pulley, and throttle body that came from the aftermarket world.
Since we mentioned the engine, we might as well tell you that the 6.8-liter supercharged V8 has undisclosed output and thrust, and works in concert with a six-speed automatic transmission.
The new fuel injectors, auxiliary fuel pump system, dual fuel pump system, air intake, exhaust headers, exhaust system, and others have also come from the tuning world. Additional modifications include the exterior lights, front grille, illuminated door handles, black rear bowtie emblem, carbon fiber pattern hydro-dipped trim, and an AEM gauge on the inside.
Some of the factory equipment includes the Magnetic Ride Control suspension, Brembo brakes, limited-slip differential, and 20-inch forged aluminum wheels. This old Chevy Camaro ZL1 also has a head-up display, heated front seats, and a power sunroof, among others.
Photo: Cars&Bids The service history is said to be detailed in the Carfax history report. The muscle car has an Ashen Gray Metallic exterior, a black cabin, and a clean Florida title. It is located in Saint Augustine, FL, and accompanied by the factory door handles, grille, two blower covers, a trunk organizer, a car cover, a set of floor mats, a carbon fiber hood insert, the window sticker, and two keys.
Interested parties should know that this Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 may not pass emissions testing in some states due to the modifications. This machine has been indeed registered to one owner in New Mexico and Florida since new, the Carfax report shows, and there are no mileage discrepancies. The car has 2024 date codes on the tires, and tinted windows.
A 2012 Chevrolet Camaro ZL1 is valued at $30,000 to $45,000 in today’s used car market. Collector grade examples, with under 10,000 miles (16,000 km), can exceed $50,000. A good daily driver with 30,000 to 60,000 miles (48,000-96,000 km) on the odo is valued at over $30,000, and high-mileage machines in rough condition cost less than $30,000.
This one definitely looks good, and the fact that it has been registered to the same person since it left the dealership back in 2012 definitely adds to the hype. Due to the modifications , however, it may not be everyone’s cup of tea, so we are curious to see how much it fetches when the gavel hits the table, because it is currently advertised on Cars&Bids as part of an ongoing online auction that will end four days from now, next Tuesday, on November 3, 2026.
At the time of writing, this Chevy Camaro ZL1 had a high bid of $6,767. There is a reserve on it, and it has obviously not been met. The owner hasn’t revealed why he wants it gone, but to be honest, he has had it for the for more than 14 years, and that’s plenty of time to get bored with every ride out there, regardless of the make and model.
Care to buy this modified muscle car? In that case, you will have to bid on it and win the online auction that you can access here on the quoted website. That is also where you can check out this Chevy Camaro ZL1 in more detail. How much is something like this worth in your opinion?
